minutes.headline: Commission approved an Oak Ridge Road septic NOI with a waiver, continued the Flat Hill garage hearing, and issued two COCs.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission, meeting by Zoom, heard a septic and retaining wall NOI at 86 Oak Ridge Road and approved it with a waiver for work in the 50-foot no-build zone and overlapping straw waddles. The 932 Flat Hill Road garage hearing was continued to the 20th with requests for tree notes and ground cover, and 205 Sunset Lane was continued to October 4. The commission issued COCs for 40 Brookfield Terrace and 91 Lancaster Ave, continued the Northfield Road Lot A COC over unclear Swale compliance, and discussed enforcement and property updates.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved a notice of intent for a septic system and retaining wall at 86 Oak Ridge Road, with a waiver for work in the 50-foot no-build zone.
The hearing on a garage at 932 Flat Hill Road was continued to the 20th, and the 205 Sunset Lane deck hearing was continued to October 4.
Certificates of compliance were approved for 40 Brookfield Terrace and 91 Lancaster Ave; the Northfield Road Lot A certificate was continued for more research on the Swale.
Approval of mushroom signs for trailhead kiosks was tabled to the next meeting so members can see the sign.
The administrator is to tell the owners at 143 Island Road to file a retroactive request for determination of applicability for tree remediation.

why_it_matters: Septic and wetland-buffer approvals like these decide what can be built near wetlands on a resident's own lot, and the compliance certificates close out earlier permits.
The retroactive filing at 143 Island Road shows the commission asking owners to file after work has been done, which bears on anyone doing tree work near a protected resource area.
watch_next: The 932 Flat Hill Road garage hearing returns on the 20th.
The 205 Sunset Lane deck hearing resumes October 4.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: All six votes match in outcome and substance, with caption errors only in "wattles" and "Brookview". The main differences are in the decisions: the 91 Lancaster tree-removal approval is described differently, ours has a 100 Hemlock item the official lacks, and the official has several site-plan and follow-up items we lack.
